answer.text: Excess return over what CAPM predicts given the portfolio's beta

explanation.text: The Logic: Jensen's Alpha is a CAPM-based performance measure defined as Rp − [Rf + β·(Rm − Rf)] — the portfolio's actual return less the return predicted by CAPM given its beta. Total return is the raw return; Sharpe ratio uses total risk (standard deviation); tracking error measures deviation from a benchmark. Note: Jensen's Alpha is not specifically defined in the PMS Distributors (XXI-A) workbook; the nearby chapters discuss alpha generation, Sharpe ratio, and benchmark-relative performance without the CAPM-alpha formula. Treat this as general portfolio-performance theory.
